6	import Mathlib

8	/-!
9	# The Jacobian challenge — statement file (with field base change)
10	
11	This is the single, self-contained **statement file** of the project: it collects every
12	definition, instance, and theorem needed to *state* the main result, and nothing else. A reviewer
13	reads this one file, compares it against the original challenge (`references/challenge.lean`, by
14	Christian Merten) and its base-change extension, and is convinced the project formalizes the right
15	thing. The genuinely-missing pieces are `sorry`; the base-change scaffolding (`baseChange`, the
16	stability instances, `idIso`, `compIso`, and `Jacobian.congr` derived from `Jacobian.functor`) is
17	genuinely proved here. Proofs of the `sorry`s live in the rest of the `AlgebraicJacobian/` tree and
18	must not weaken or restate any signature below.
19	
20	By a **smooth curve** we mean a geometrically irreducible, smooth scheme of relative dimension one
21	over a field, proper over that field.
22	
23	## Main definitions
24	
25	* `AlgebraicGeometry.genus` — genus of a proper, smooth curve.
26	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian` — the Jacobian of a proper, smooth curve.
27	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian.ofCurve` — the Abel–Jacobi map associated to a `k`-rational point.
28	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian.functor` — functoriality of the Jacobian, bundled as a single
29	  contravariant functor `(Curve k)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Grp (Over (Spec k))`.
30	
31	## Main theorems
32	
33	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian.smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus` — the Jacobian is smooth of relative
34	  dimension `g = genus C`.
35	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian.exists_unique_ofCurve_comp` — the universal property: the Jacobian is
36	  the Albanese variety of `C`.
37	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian.baseChangeIso` — the Jacobian commutes with base change of fields,
38	  together with the identity/cocycle coherences (`baseChangeIso_id`, `baseChangeIso_comp`) and the
39	  Abel–Jacobi compatibility `baseChange_ofCurve`.
40	
41	## Notes
42	
43	`noncomputable` is on the data-carrying declarations: their honest realizations rest on
44	noncomputable Mathlib constructions. Names, argument types, and argument order are verbatim from
45	the challenge; the `noncomputable` modifier is not a signature change.
46	-/
47	
48	set_option autoImplicit false
49	
50	universe u
51	
52	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory MonObj
53	
54	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
55	
56	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
57	  -- smooth curve
58	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom]
59	  -- proper
60	  [IsProper C.hom]
61	  -- geometrically irreducible
62	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
63	
64	/-- The category of smooth, proper, geometrically irreducible curves over `k`, with morphisms the
65	morphisms of `k`-schemes. -/
66	structure Curve (k : Type u) [Field k] where
67	  /-- The underlying `k`-scheme. -/
68	  carrier : Over (Spec (.of k))
69	  [isProper : IsProper carrier.hom]
70	  [smoothOfRelativeDimension : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 carrier.hom]
71	  [geometricallyIrreducible : GeometricallyIrreducible carrier.hom]
72	
73	attribute [instance] Curve.isProper Curve.smoothOfRelativeDimension Curve.geometricallyIrreducible
74	
75	noncomputable instance (k : Type u) [Field k] : Category (Curve k) where
76	  Hom X Y := X.carrier ⟶ Y.carrier
77	  id X := 𝟙 X.carrier
78	  comp f g := f ≫ g
79	  id_comp := Category.id_comp
80	  comp_id := Category.comp_id
81	  assoc := Category.assoc
82	
83	-- data
84	/-- The genus of a smooth proper curve. -/
85	noncomputable def genus (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
86	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] : ℕ :=
87	  sorry
88	
89	-- data
90	/-- The Jacobian of a smooth, proper curve over a field `k`. -/
91	noncomputable def Jacobian (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
92	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
93	    Over (Spec (.of k)) :=
94	  sorry
95	
96	namespace Jacobian
97	
98	/-! ## The Jacobian of `C` is an abelian variety. -/
99	
100	-- data
101	/-- The group scheme structure on the Jacobian of the curve `C`. -/
102	noncomputable instance instGrpObj : GrpObj (Jacobian C) :=
103	  sorry
104	
105	/-- The Jacobian of `C` is smooth of relative dimension `g` over `k`, where `g` is the
106	genus of `C`. -/
107	instance smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus : SmoothOfRelativeDimension (genus C) (Jacobian C).hom :=
108	  sorry
109	
110	/-- The Jacobian of `C` is proper over `k`. -/
111	instance : IsProper (Jacobian C).hom :=
112	  sorry
113	
114	/-- The Jacobian of `C` is geometrically irreducible over `k`. -/
115	instance : GeometricallyIrreducible (Jacobian C).hom :=
116	  sorry
117	
118	/-- The Abel-Jacobi map from a smooth, proper curve to its Jacobian associated
119	to a `k`-rational point of `C`. -/
120	noncomputable def ofCurve (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C) : C ⟶ Jacobian C :=
121	  sorry
122	
123	/-- The Abel-Jacobi map sends the `k`-rational point `P` to `0`, where `0` (denoted by `η`) is the
124	neutral element of the group scheme `Jacobian C`. -/
125	theorem comp_ofCurve (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
126	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
127	    (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C) :
128	    P ≫ ofCurve P = η[Jacobian C] :=
129	  sorry
130	
131	/--
132	The universal property of the Jacobian variety: For any abelian variety `A`, any morphism
133	`f : C ⟶ A` with `f(P) = 0` factors uniquely through the Jacobian of `C`. In other words,
134	`Jacobian C` is the Albanese variety of `C`.
135	-/
136	theorem exists_unique_ofCurve_comp (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
137	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
138	    (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C)
139	    {A : Over (Spec (.of k))} [Smooth A.hom] [IsProper A.hom] [GrpObj A]
140	    [GeometricallyIrreducible A.hom] (f : C ⟶ A) (hf : P ≫ f = η[A]) :
141	    ∃! (g : Jacobian C ⟶ A), f = ofCurve P ≫ g :=
142	  sorry
143	
144	/-- **Functoriality of the Jacobian**, bundled as a single contravariant functor: a curve goes to
145	its Jacobian group scheme over `k`, and a morphism of curves to the pullback of line bundles. The
146	functor laws (`map_id`, `map_comp`) are embedded in this `Functor`. The object action is pinned to
147	the `Jacobian` above, so everything downstream stays phrased in terms of `Jacobian C`. -/
148	noncomputable def functor (k : Type u) [Field k] :
149	    (Curve k)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Grp (Over (Spec (.of k))) where
150	  obj X := .mk (Jacobian X.unop.carrier)
151	  map _ := sorry
152	  map_id := sorry
153	  map_comp := sorry
154	
155	end Jacobian
156	
157	/-! ## Base change of fields
158	
159	Base change of `k`-schemes along `k → L` sends `X` to `X ×_{Spec k} Spec L`. These definitions and
160	the stability instances are genuine (no `sorry`); they set up the statements of the base-change
161	compatibility of the Jacobian. -/
162	
163	/-- Base change of `k`-schemes along a field homomorphism `k → L`, i.e. `X ↦ X ×_{Spec k} Spec L`.
164	-/
165	noncomputable abbrev baseChange (k L : Type u) [Field k] [Field L] [Algebra k L] :
166	    Over (Spec (.of k)) ⥤ Over (Spec (.of L)) :=
167	  Over.pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L)))
168	
169	instance {k L : Type u} [Field k] [Field L] [Algebra k L] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
170	    [IsProper C.hom] : IsProper ((baseChange k L).obj C).hom :=
171	  MorphismProperty.baseChange_obj (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L))) C inferInstance
172	
173	instance {k L : Type u} [Field k] [Field L] [Algebra k L] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
174	    [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] : GeometricallyIrreducible ((baseChange k L).obj C).hom :=
175	  MorphismProperty.baseChange_obj (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L))) C inferInstance
176	
177	instance {k L : Type u} [Field k] [Field L] [Algebra k L] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
178	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] :
179	    SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 ((baseChange k L).obj C).hom :=
180	  have : MorphismProperty.IsStableUnderBaseChange (@SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1) :=
181	    smoothOfRelativeDimension_isStableUnderBaseChange 1
182	  MorphismProperty.baseChange_obj (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L))) C inferInstance
183	
184	-- The coherences mention curves of the form `(𝟭 _).obj C` and `(F ⋙ G).obj C`.
185	instance {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom] :
186	    IsProper ((𝟭 (Over (Spec (.of k)))).obj C).hom := ‹_›
187	instance {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
188	    GeometricallyIrreducible ((𝟭 (Over (Spec (.of k)))).obj C).hom := ‹_›
189	instance {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] :
190	    SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 ((𝟭 (Over (Spec (.of k)))).obj C).hom := ‹_›
191	
192	instance {k L M : Type u} [Field k] [Field L] [Field M] [Algebra k L] [Algebra L M]
193	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom] :
194	    IsProper ((baseChange k L ⋙ baseChange L M).obj C).hom :=
195	  inferInstanceAs (IsProper ((baseChange L M).obj ((baseChange k L).obj C)).hom)
196	instance {k L M : Type u} [Field k] [Field L] [Field M] [Algebra k L] [Algebra L M]
197	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
198	    GeometricallyIrreducible ((baseChange k L ⋙ baseChange L M).obj C).hom :=
199	  inferInstanceAs (GeometricallyIrreducible ((baseChange L M).obj ((baseChange k L).obj C)).hom)
200	instance {k L M : Type u} [Field k] [Field L] [Field M] [Algebra k L] [Algebra L M]
201	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] :
202	    SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 ((baseChange k L ⋙ baseChange L M).obj C).hom :=
203	  inferInstanceAs (SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 ((baseChange L M).obj ((baseChange k L).obj C)).hom)
204	
205	/-- Base change along `k → k` is the identity functor. -/
206	noncomputable def baseChange.idIso (k : Type u) [Field k] :
207	    baseChange k k ≅ 𝟭 (Over (Spec (.of k))) :=
208	  eqToIso (by
209	    change Over.pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k k))) = Over.pullback (𝟙 _)
210	    rw [Algebra.algebraMap_self, CommRingCat.ofHom_id, Spec.map_id]) ≪≫ Over.pullbackId
211	
212	/-- Base change along a tower `k → L → M` is the composite of the two base changes. -/
213	noncomputable def baseChange.compIso (k L M : Type u) [Field k] [Field L] [Field M]
214	    [Algebra k L] [Algebra L M] [Algebra k M] [IsScalarTower k L M] :
215	    baseChange k M ≅ baseChange k L ⋙ baseChange L M :=
216	  eqToIso (by
217	    change Over.pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k M))) =
218	      Over.pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap L M)) ≫
219	        Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L)))
220	    rw [← Spec.map_comp, ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp, ← IsScalarTower.algebraMap_eq]) ≪≫
221	    Over.pullbackComp _ _
222	
223	namespace Jacobian
224	
225	/-- The Jacobian respects isomorphisms of curves — *derived* from the bundled functor
226	`Jacobian.functor` via `Functor.mapIso`, not a primitive. Used to compare the two sides of the
227	cocycle, whose curves agree only up to `baseChange.compIso`. -/
228	noncomputable def congr {k : Type u} [Field k] {C C' : Over (Spec (.of k))}
229	    [IsProper C.hom] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
230	    [IsProper C'.hom] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C'.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C'.hom]
231	    (e : C ≅ C') :
232	    (.mk (Jacobian C) : Grp (Over (Spec (.of k)))) ≅ .mk (Jacobian C') :=
233	  let j : (⟨C⟩ : Curve k) ≅ ⟨C'⟩ :=
234	    { hom := e.hom, inv := e.inv, hom_inv_id := e.hom_inv_id, inv_hom_id := e.inv_hom_id }
235	  (Jacobian.functor k).mapIso j.symm.op
236	
237	/-- **The base-change condition.** Jacobians commute with base change of fields: a canonical
238	isomorphism `Jac(C)_L ≅ Jac(C_L)`, as group schemes over `L`. -/
239	noncomputable def baseChangeIso (k L : Type u) [Field k] [Field L] [Algebra k L]
240	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
241	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
242	    (baseChange k L).mapGrp.obj (.mk (Jacobian C)) ≅ .mk (Jacobian ((baseChange k L).obj C)) :=
243	  sorry
244	
245	/-! ## Functoriality: the base change isomorphisms form a coherent system. -/
246	
247	/-- Identity coherence. -/
248	theorem baseChangeIso_id (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
249	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
250	    baseChangeIso k k C =
251	      (Functor.mapGrpNatIso (baseChange.idIso k)).app _
252	        ≪≫ (Functor.mapGrpIdIso (C := Over (Spec (.of k)))).app _
253	        ≪≫ Jacobian.congr ((baseChange.idIso k).app C).symm :=
254	  sorry
255	
256	/-- Cocycle coherence for a tower `k → L → M`. -/
257	theorem baseChangeIso_comp (k L M : Type u) [Field k] [Field L] [Field M]
258	    [Algebra k L] [Algebra L M] [Algebra k M] [IsScalarTower k L M]
259	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
260	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
261	    baseChangeIso k M C
262	        ≪≫ Jacobian.congr ((baseChange.compIso k L M).app C) =
263	      (Functor.mapGrpNatIso (baseChange.compIso k L M)).app _
264	        ≪≫ (Functor.mapGrpCompIso (F := baseChange k L) (G := baseChange L M)).app _
265	        ≪≫ (baseChange L M).mapGrp.mapIso (baseChangeIso k L C)
266	        ≪≫ baseChangeIso L M ((baseChange k L).obj C) :=
267	  sorry
268	
269	/-! ## Compatibility with the Abel-Jacobi map -/
270	
271	variable {L : Type u} [Field L] [Algebra k L]
272	
273	theorem baseChange_ofCurve (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
274	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
275	    (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C) :
276	    (baseChange k L).map (ofCurve P) ≫ (baseChangeIso k L C).hom.hom.hom =
277	      ofCurve (Functor.LaxMonoidal.ε (baseChange k L) ≫ (baseChange k L).map P) :=
278	  sorry
279	
280	end Jacobian
281	
282	end AlgebraicGeometry

1	# AlgebraicJacobian (rebuild)
2	
3	<!-- archon:readme -->
4	
5	## Project
6	
7	A **from-scratch rebuild** of the Lean 4 + Mathlib formalization of the **Jacobian of a smooth,
8	proper, geometrically irreducible curve** over a field (Christian Merten's AI challenge, inspired by
9	Kevin Buzzard's Riemann-surface version). By a smooth curve we mean a geometrically irreducible,
10	smooth scheme of relative dimension one over a field.
11	
12	This project supplies the missing definitions (`genus`, `Jacobian`, the Abel–Jacobi map `ofCurve`)
13	and theorems (the Jacobian is smooth of relative dimension equal to the genus, proper, geometrically
14	irreducible, and is the Albanese variety of the curve, characterized by the universal property
15	`exists_unique_ofCurve_comp`). It targets the **extended** challenge: additionally, the Jacobian is
16	**functorial** in the curve (`Jacobian.functor`) and **commutes with base change of fields**
17	(`baseChangeIso` with identity and cocycle coherences, and Abel–Jacobi compatibility
18	`baseChange_ofCurve`), which makes the construction canonical.
19	
20	It is rebuilt rather than continued: the goal is a cleaner, more general, mathlib-idiomatic
21	infrastructure and a shorter, clearer path to the conclusion. The existing project
22	`MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge` may be **read** when genuinely blocked, but nothing is
23	copied from it — every declaration is rewritten. The rebuild is driven by its Archon Horizon task,
24	which carries the full charter (target, constraints, working model, and phases).
25	
26	## Structure
27	
28	- `AlgebraicJacobian/Challenge.lean` — the single, reviewable **statement file**: every signature a
29	  reviewer must trust, and nothing else. Agents own the proofs, never these signatures.
30	- `AlgebraicJacobian/` — the infrastructure that discharges the statement (added as the rebuild
31	  proceeds; no file exceeds 500 lines; layout mirrors the mathematical structure of the paper).
32	- `AlgebraicJacobian.lean` — the library root import list.
33	- `blueprint/` — a clean **mathematical** blueprint (no Lean code in the prose; nodes carry `\lean{}`
34	  and `\source{}` anchors). Build with `leanblueprint pdf` / `leanblueprint web`.
35	- `archon-protected.yaml` — the mathematician-owned signatures agents must not modify.
36	
37	## Sources
38	
39	The shared workspace-root [`references/`](../../references/) library (indexed by
40	`references/manifest.yaml`) backs the blueprint. Read a source before citing it with `\source{...}`.
41	
42	## How to build
43	
44	```bash
45	lake build           # compile (olean cache shared via ../../.lake-packages)
46	```

Base directory for this skill: /home/Axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/.claude/skills/task-status

A task is the unit of work a run dispatches. **You own its outcome.** The
orchestrator/scheduler only ever writes `queued` and `running`; it never reads
your report and never marks a task `done`, `blocked`, or `failed` for you. If you
do not record a terminal status, the task simply returns to `queued` for the next
round. Record status through the CLI — invoke it via the `$HORIZON_BIN` env var
(an absolute path); a bare `horizon` may not be on your shell's PATH.

## The labels

- `queued` — runnable. The scheduler picks up only queued tasks. This is where a
  task rests between rounds when work remains. **Set by the machine (and humans);
  you normally don't.**
- `running` — a session is actively driving it right now. **Set by the machine at
  dispatch.** Don't set this yourself — it means "another session is live," and
  the CLI refuses to start a second run of a `running` task.
- `done` — the assigned objective is **FULLY complete**: the Lean is proved and
  builds, the blueprint node(s) are closed, nothing in the objective remains. Not
  "mostly done", not "the hard part is done", not "a clean commit landed". **Only
  you can set this, and only when it is genuinely, completely finished.** Ground
  verifies it against the diff and the Lean state and will flip a premature `done`
  back — so a false `done` wastes a round, it doesn't save one.
- `blocked` — you cannot make progress: a dependency is missing, a decision is
  needed, or an external constraint stops you. Say why in a comment.
- `failed` — you genuinely could not do the work (not merely "ran out of time" —
  that's just `queued` for next round). Say why in a comment.
- `cancelled` — abandoned by a human. You won't normally set this.

## How to set status

```
"$HORIZON_BIN" task set <task_id> --status done      # objective FULLY complete
"$HORIZON_BIN" task set <task_id> --status blocked   # stuck; explain in a comment
"$HORIZON_BIN" task set <task_id> --status failed    # could not do it; explain
```

Authorship is automatic — the CLI stamps your role (`ground`/`horizon`) from the
run environment; do not pass `--author`. Setting a status appends an auditable
history entry, and if the task has `roadmap_refs` the linked roadmap items are
synced (done→done, blocked/failed→blocked, cancelled→rejected).

Base directory for this skill: /home/Axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/.claude/skills/blueprint-conventions

Blueprints are a LaTeX subset (the `leanblueprint` dialect) parsed into the DAG.
Write timeless mathematics — a standalone document, not a project journal.

## Environments

Each declaration is an amsthm-style environment; the recognized ones are
`theorem`, `lemma`, `proposition`, `corollary`, `definition`, `remark`,
`example`, `notation`, `convention`, and `proof`. A statement environment plus
its following `proof` environment form one node's content.

## Per-node macros

- `\label{id}` — a stable id (the DAG node key).
- `\lean{Name}` — the Lean declaration this node formalizes. Keep it 1-to-1: one
  blueprint node ↔ one Lean declaration, signatures matching.
- `\uses{a,b}` — dependencies on other nodes' labels; these drive the DAG edges.
  Add an edge instead of re-explaining a dependency in prose. Put `\uses` in the
  statement for definitional deps and in the `proof` for deps used only in the
  proof.
- `\source{slug:page-0001}` — reference anchors for UI popups and audit trails.
  Use page-level ids from `references/<slug>/tex/page-0001.tex` or an equivalent
  manifest entry. Multiple anchors may be comma-separated.
- `\leanok` — the Lean is written and checked. Honest only when its Lean is
  actually checked *and* its dependencies are too. On a `proof`, it means the
  proof is formalized; on a statement, the signature is formalized.
- `\mathlibok` — the declaration is already available in mathlib (no
  formalization needed; treat as a leaf).

## House style

- **Pure mathematics only.** No Lean tactics, typeclass/implementation notes, or
  semi-Lean pseudocode. No project history ("since iter N", "our failed route")
  and no conversational filler. If a Lean helper exists with no math counterpart,
  write its LaTeX statement so the 1-to-1 correspondence holds.
- **Complete proofs, not sketches.** A node's `proof` is a real, rigorous
  mathematical proof a reader could check — not a hand-wave or a TODO. The way to
  keep it short is to *split*, not to abbreviate: if a proof is long or a node
  grows past a short paragraph, break out the hard step as its own `\uses`-linked
  lemma (down to sentence-sized lemmas if needed) so each node stays small and
  its proof stays complete.
- **One declaration's worth per node.** Don't restate Lean source as prose.
- **Cite by source link, not quote comments.** Add `\source{...}` to the
  relevant node. Keep the retrieved/transcribed page text in `references/` (for
  example `references/<slug>/tex/page-0042.tex`) and let the UI expose it; do not
  paste verbatim source quotes into `% QUOTE` comments inside the blueprint.

Base directory for this skill: /home/Axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/.claude/skills/references

`references/` is a **shared library at the workspace root** — one library for
every project — holding the original source material a blueprint is formalised
from (papers, books, notes). It is indexed by `references/manifest.yaml`. Per-
project files live under each project's directory; `references/` does not — it is
always at the workspace root, and `references/**` is writable from any agent.

A blueprint node derived from a source carries a `\source{...}` anchor. Those
anchors are the audit trail from a formal statement back to where it came from,
so they must be **true**, not plausible.

## The one rule: read before you cite

**Never add a `\source{...}` anchor to a source you have not actually read.** Do
not infer a citation from a title, a topic, a theorem number, or your own prior
knowledge of the result. An anchor asserts "this exact statement/proof appears
here" — if you haven't opened the referenced material and confirmed it, you don't
know that, and a wrong anchor is worse than none (it sends the next reader/agent
to the wrong place and launders a guess as provenance).

Concretely, before writing `\source{...}`:
1. Confirm the source exists in `references/manifest.yaml`. If it isn't there,
   get it in first (see below) — don't cite a slug that doesn't resolve.

## Anchor forms — pick by what the source actually is

The manifest's `read` field for each entry tells you which case you're in.

- **The source has LaTeX** (arXiv e-print, an open `.tex`, etc.): read the TeX
  directly and cite the source as a whole — `\source{slug}`. Do **not** invent a

  been transcribed yet, transcribe it first (below) — don't cite a page that

Don't fetch and stash sources ad hoc. Spawn the **`reference-retriever`** subagent
(by name, through your engine's native subagent mechanism) with whatever you have

page named `.pdf`), organises it under `references/<slug>/`, and registers it in

When there is no reliable TeX and you need the actual math (to read it, or to cite
a page), **extract it with the proper tool — don't eyeball the PDF and paraphrase.**

  rule of the transcription flow.
- **A small vision model is usually enough.** Faithful page transcription doesn't
  need a frontier model — a cheap vision-capable model (e.g. Haiku) running in the
  background typically suffices, which is what the config is for:

  ```yaml

    transcription:
      harness: <optional harness>
      model: <cheap vision-capable model, e.g. a Haiku-class model>

  uses the same cheap vision model. When unset it falls back to the subagent/Ground

  across several `page-transcriber` calls.

- A transcribed page is `references/<slug>/tex/page-NNNN.tex` where `NNNN` is the
  **PDF page index**, which often differs from the printed page number. The
  manifest entry's `read` field records the `page_offset` and any fallback that

- Read the whole page file before citing it; a page can hold several results.

```yaml
references:
  - slug: <slug>
    title: <title>
    source: <arXiv ID / DOI / URL>
    status: ok            # or: not_found
    files:
      - { path: <slug>/<slug>.pdf, format: pdf }
      - { path: <slug>/source.tex, format: tex }        # if TeX obtained
      - { path: <slug>/tex/page-0042.tex, format: tex } # if transcribed
    read: "Read TeX when present; else page anchors slug:page-NNNN. page_offset: ..."
```

If a source can't be found and verified, it's recorded `status: not_found` — treat
